items.says: The feature-store result is hidden after a long sequence of implementation details.
Sunrise Bakery appears before the quantitative roles, making retail look like the candidate's primary direction.
The quantitative projects are separated from Northpeak Capital instead of reinforcing the visible research and modeling trajectory.
“Within its weekly labour budget” does not show how closely labour spending matched the budget.
“Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders” does not say what changed in the ordering process and makes supplier orders sound counted rather than placed.
“Keeping 90% of gross returns” does not identify the return measure or comparison behind the retention figure.
Standard Diebold–Mariano tests do not by themselves validly confirm a forecast gain against a nested HAR-RV model across 30 indices.
The bullet says the forecast gain was confirmed without stating how large the gain was or what changed.
“Nested HAR-RV baseline” and “Diebold-Mariano tests” obscure the plain-language result for a general reader.
The construction “Joining 120 microstructure features ... built” is grammatically incorrect and leaves the subject of the work unclear.
The daily Sharpe ratio was annualized with the wrong factor: daily Sharpe ratios scale by the square root of time, not by 252.
Multiplying the daily Sharpe ratio by 252 provides no performance comparison, validation result or downstream measure.
The wiki's onboarding use is stated without showing what improvement it produced.
The onboarding result is placed at the end after several documentation details.
A seed and configuration file alone do not guarantee that every shared-cluster run is reproducible.
The phrase “my proof” violates the résumé's phrase-style bullet format.
The bound improvement is stated without the exact old-versus-new bound or asymptotic comparison.
The phrase “is now Section 3 of a paper” is awkward and makes the publication status harder to scan.
The teaching bullet describes recitations and problem sets without showing the instructional method or learning result.
The final bullet bundles the package, cluster, reading group and grading into an unordered task list.
The R package is named without indicating the distinctive technical work implemented inside it.
The package's 3,000-download result is grammatically separated from the product it measures.
The reduction from 0.20 to 0.15 is a 25% reduction, not a 33% improvement.
“Forecast error” does not identify the metric that changed from 0.20 to 0.15.
The second volatility-study bullet repeats “adding realized-volatility features” without showing that it was a separate experiment.
The change from 52% to 58% is an increase of 6 percentage points, not 6%.
The competition placement and top-2% statement communicate nearly the same result.
The 0.02 gap is not identified by metric or described with a clear before-and-after comparison.
“Cut validation leakage” is abstract, and the measurable score-gap reduction is buried after the method.
“Without losing validation score” does not name the metric or state the comparison with the 900-feature model.
